newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Finance Minister slams pessimism.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Finance Minister slams pessimism.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Monday an "obsession for pessimism" was preventing the country from detecting the signs of economic recovery.
"Because of this obsession for pessimism the signs (for the economy) are not being perceived," Ocampo told reporters in the Caribbean port city of Cartagena.

The finance minister was speaking just hours after the National Statistics Department released May inflation figures showing the consumer price index rose 1.62 percent, compared to 1.55 percent in May 1996.

Despite the slight year-on-year increase, Ocampo pointed to total inflation of 9.94 percent in the first five months of the year compared to 12.75 percent in the same period last year. The central bank target is for 18 percent inflation in 1997.

Last week, however, the government announced first quarter gross domestic product posted -1.22 percent negative growth, signaling the country's first recession in decades when coupled with -0.1 percent negative growth in the final quarter of 1996.

But Ocampo said high international coffee prices, further proposed cuts in interest rates and a recovery in the economies of Colombia's main Latin American trading partners would help the country return to growth.
